tasks.short: Maintain accurate logistics records and supporting documents under corporate policies.

steps.what: Collect shipment events and supporting documents.
Check identifiers, required fields and supporting documents against record rules.
Resolve missing evidence and conflicting shipment details with operational colleagues.
Approve material corrections under the record policy.
Update logistics records and link the supporting evidence.
File supporting documents with retention labels and access permissions.

tasks.design: A connector collects shipment events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and financial references from the {ERP}; deterministic checks create an exception queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Validated updates write automatically, while material corrections require the supervisor's recorded approval before writing; the approval from s4 is reused in s5. Configure evidence links, permissions and retention labels in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Identifiers differ across records, evidence sits separately, and correction rules are often implicit. Connecting the systems previously cost more than repetitive entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Available exports or interfaces support repeatable checks and controlled writes. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building mappings, forms and reconciliation checks; no model loop is needed here.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting evidence and historical corrections still need operational knowledge. Personal data in delivery evidence requires GDPR controls; employee monitoring would require separate assessment under EU law and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Establish which account of a shipment is credible and recognise corrections that could conceal a service failure.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of unresolved shipment records by operational and financial impact.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time copying records and more time resolving evidence gaps. With delegated correction limits, the analyst can close routine discrepancies; material corrections remain with the supervisor.

reach.task: Resolve recurring receipt and delivery record discrepancies.
reach.learn: Warehouse event meanings, proof-of-delivery practices and stock reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Structured logistics records can use deterministic validation, controlled updates and evidence links.
Local savings and the share of corrections requiring approval remain unmeasured.

assumptions: This baseline describes a mid-size European company with operational records already held in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Supporting documents are partly separate from transaction records; a spreadsheet is not assumed to be the main register.
Material corrections require supervisor approval; routine validated updates do not.
Time shares and remaining percentages are design estimates, not measured results.
Build ranges cover one initial record flow; consultation may extend elapsed time where national rules apply.
unknowns: Which interfaces, stable shipment identifiers and write permissions are available?
Which corrections require approval, and who may approve them?
What retention periods, legal holds and access rules apply?
Does shipment evidence identify employees or support employee monitoring?
How complete and reliable are current shipment events?
research_questions: Which validation rules catch the largest recurring discrepancy categories?
Can native evidence linking and retention configuration replace custom document handling?
What reconciliation proves that each accepted update was written exactly once?
new_work: Resolve rejected updates and missing evidence.
Review sampled automatic updates and investigate reconciliation failures.
Maintain field mappings, correction thresholds and retention rules.
Manage interface credentials, access changes and applicable employee consultation.

tasks.short: Obtain carrier rates and schedules, clarify conditions, and record comparable options.

steps.what: Define shipment requirements and acceptable collection and delivery windows.
Check existing carrier rates and published schedules before requesting new information.
Send rate and schedule enquiries to suitable carriers.
Read carrier replies and capture rates, schedules, exclusions and validity dates.

loop.input: Carrier reply text and attachments, linked to the rate request brief.
loop.output: Draft quote fields with source passages and explicit missing-value flags.
loop.check: Validate currency, units, dates and required fields; show source passages for analyst review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per reply; unresolved or unsupported fields go to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text replies and attachments express surcharges, exclusions and availability inconsistently; structured replies bypass the loop.

steps.what: Compare total charges and schedule fit on a common basis.
Clarify availability and discuss unusual conditions with carriers.
Record confirmed rates and schedules for shipment planning.

tasks.design: Build a request form from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, retrieve available rates from the {PROCUREMENT} and accessible {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and send nonbinding enquiries through the {EMAIL}. A bounded extraction loop turns unstructured replies into draft quote records; deterministic calculations compare total charges and schedule fit. The analyst handles clarification calls and approves confirmed terms before they enter the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Carrier information arrives through different channels and uses inconsistent units and conditions. One-off enquiries rarely justified dedicated integration work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors and calculation rules cover structured information. A small extraction loop can handle variable reply formats without delegating negotiation or booking.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity can change before a shipment is booked. Conditional surcharges and informal promises still need confirmation, and some carriers offer no usable interface.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a carrier's promise is credible and secure practical arrangements for unusual shipments.

ambition.what: Same-day comparable carrier options for occasional shipment planners.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time chasing standard information and more time resolving capacity and service trade-offs. The analyst can shortlist options within agreed criteria; contracting and booking rights do not change.

reach.task: Assess whether quoted collection windows fit the dispatch plan.
reach.learn: Loading constraints, cut-off times and practical recovery options.

reach.task: Prepare lane tender requirements from recurring quote gaps.
reach.learn: Carrier qualification, capacity commitments and tender evaluation.

evidence.claim: Deterministic request templates, quote calculations and expiry checks can reduce enquiry administration.
Transporeon checks carrier invoices against agreed rates, supporting the feasibility of structured freight-rate checks.
Extracting arbitrary carrier replies and retrieving local carrier schedules require separate validation.

assumptions: A meaningful share of enquiries still uses the {EMAIL} and telephone; portal access varies by carrier.
Existing valid rates remove some enquiries entirely.
Automatic messages use approved recipients and minimum shipment details, and create no commitment.
Booking, contract acceptance and payment are outside this task.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for a small initial carrier set.
unknowns: Which carriers provide interfaces, structured files or permitted portal access?
What proportion of replies are structured, free text or telephone-only?
Who may request quotes, negotiate conditions and accept a booking?
Which charge components, currencies and service definitions must be compared?
What personal or commercially sensitive information appears in replies?
research_questions: Can a standard reply form remove extraction for frequently contacted carriers?
Which quote fields produce the most consequential comparison errors?
How should quote expiry and unconfirmed capacity appear to shipment planners?
new_work: Review extracted exclusions, units and validity dates.
Confirm ambiguous terms and handle unanswered enquiries.
Maintain carrier contacts, calculation rules and interface mappings.
Monitor extraction errors and maintain GDPR-compliant handling of reply data.

tasks.short: Keep logistics pricing structures aligned with actual costs and approved commercial choices.

steps.what: Collect shipment activity, carrier charges and current pricing tables.
Reconcile charges and flag missing or inconsistent cost inputs.
Allocate logistics costs and calculate recovery under alternative pricing structures.
Choose a proposed allocation method and pricing changes with commercial colleagues.
Approve pricing changes, allocation rules and effective dates within delegated authority.
Publish approved pricing tables and verify sample calculations.
Check realised cost recovery after pricing changes take effect.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile {ERP} charges with {OPS_SYSTEM} activity and calculate versioned allocation and pricing scenarios for the {BI}. A version-specific approval in the {WORKFLOW} gates effective-dated pricing writes to the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}, reusing the decision from s5. Reconciliation checks and a variance dashboard detect publication errors and weak cost recovery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs and prices use different units, periods and allocation assumptions. Fragile workbook links make frequent recalculation expensive, while the allocation method remains a business choice.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned calculation code, repeatable imports and automated reconciliation make updates easier to build and test. This requires explicit cost definitions rather than a model breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Late invoices, shared capacity and volatile surcharges complicate cost attribution. Commercial teams must decide which costs to recover and when contracts permit price changes.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible allocation methods and balance cost recovery against service commitments and customer relationships.

ambition.what: Weekly lane-level surcharge adjustment proposals after material cost movements.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time explaining cost drivers and testing pricing choices. The target role can initiate repricing proposals against agreed thresholds; final pricing approval remains with the authorised manager.

reach.task: Assess lane consolidation and carrier changes using cost-to-serve scenarios.
reach.learn: Network constraints, capacity commitments and service trade-offs.

reach.task: Compare cost allocation methods across operating units.
reach.learn: Activity-based costing, sensitivity analysis and financial reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Transporeon checks freight invoices against agreed rates; this supports rate validation, not automatic commercial pricing decisions.
Cost allocation and pricing scenario calculations can use deterministic code once definitions and rules are explicit.

assumptions: The analyst maintains logistics charges or cost-based pricing inputs, rather than setting all customer prices.
A finance manager has delegated approval authority for the initial pricing scope.
Approval binds to the exact proposed version, effective date and destination; publication does not require a second approval.
Initial calculations use shipment and cost data without individual employee performance scoring.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one pricing structure and a limited system scope.
unknowns: Where are authoritative pricing tables held, and which systems consume them?
How are handling, empty mileage, storage and shared capacity allocated?
Which costs arrive late, and how are accruals treated?
Who has pricing approval authority, and what contractual notice periods apply?
Can the destination systems support effective dates, rollback and version checks?
research_questions: Which existing pricing configuration can replace custom calculations or publication code?
Which historical invoices and shipments provide representative reconciliation cases?
How sensitive are recommendations to allocation assumptions and missing cost inputs?
new_work: Resolve unmatched costs and maintain allocation definitions.
Review scenario sensitivity and explain proposed changes.
Maintain regression examples for rates, rounding and effective dates.
Monitor pricing writes, reconciliation failures and realised cost recovery.
Review access and approval limits when responsibilities change.

tasks.short: Agree logistics improvements with management using service, efficiency and cost evidence.

steps.what: Assemble service, capacity and cost measures for the management review.
Model service and cost options under stated operational constraints.
Prepare a concise review pack showing options, assumptions and unresolved questions.
Discuss trade-offs, operational concerns and feasible improvement options.
Authorise a pilot with service limits, spending limits and accountable owners.
Record agreed actions, owners and review dates.

tasks.design: Connect the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} to a governed dataset and a scenario dashboard in the {BI}; generate a review pack in the {DOCS} from explicit assumptions and calculations. Management discusses the trade-offs and authorises pilots, recording decisions through a structured form in the {WORKFLOW}. Approved decisions create actions in the {PROJECT} and review dates in the {CALENDAR}, without automatically changing live operations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing comparable evidence takes time, and each discussion often starts from a different workbook. Tacit operating constraints prevent a purely numerical answer.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable datasets, scenario calculations and document templates reduce preparation effort. Structured decision capture removes follow-up transcription without requiring meeting recording or an autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Models can omit operational constraints, and teams may disagree about acceptable service risk. Pilot results need interpretation before wider adoption; worker-affecting changes may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Surface hidden constraints, resolve competing priorities and build commitment to a change that teams can execute.

ambition.what: Fortnightly selection of a reversible lane-level service or cost pilot.

tasks.altitude: Preparation becomes shorter, while discussion and accountability remain central to the week. With delegated limits, the analyst can initiate and stop small pilots against agreed service thresholds; management retains wider rollout and spending decisions.

reach.task: Run a logistics pilot with milestones and a benefits review.
reach.learn: Experiment design, dependency management and benefit attribution.

reach.task: Test recovery options for a disrupted transport lane.
reach.learn: Recovery priorities, fallback capacity and disruption exercises.

evidence.claim: ORTEC documents route planning for Albert Heijn, showing practical use of routing technology; the case does not establish local savings.
Deterministic scenario calculations and templated review packs can support management discussions without automating the discussion.
Pilot authority, preparation savings and the value of more frequent reviews require local validation.

assumptions: Discussion and decisions occupy most of the task; preparation remains open to automation.
Initial scenarios cover a few explicit hypotheses rather than a complete supply-chain optimiser.
The review pack uses tables, charts and templated statements; no model-written recommendation is required.
Structured decision capture supplies owners, limits and dates without recording the meeting.
Build ranges cover the decision-support workflow, not implementing operational changes.
Consultation time depends on the proposed pilot and applicable national rules; build days exclude waiting for a consultation timetable.
unknowns: Which service measures and cost definitions does management trust?
Which operational constraints are absent from current data?
Who can authorise pilots, stop them and approve wider rollout?
Which proposed changes affect staffing, work organisation or employee monitoring?
What systems hold actions and pilot outcome evidence?
research_questions: Which recurring management decision would benefit most from a reusable scenario?
What baseline and comparison method can distinguish pilot effects from seasonal changes?
Can a structured decision form capture follow-up work during the meeting?
new_work: Maintain scenario assumptions and test them against operating experience.
Investigate data quality warnings before management reviews.
Measure pilot outcomes and document reasons for stopping or expanding them.
Maintain action templates, decision permissions and dashboard definitions.
Assess GDPR and EU AI Act applicability when scope changes, and arrange employee consultation where national rules require it.

role.altitude: The logistics analyst becomes a steward of reliable operating evidence and a designer of bounded improvement trials. Proposed new authority covers routine corrections and small pilots within delegated limits; commercial commitments, material pricing changes and wider operational changes retain named approvers.
reach: Help shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks eliminate recurring record discrepancies.
Help dispatchers compare feasible carrier options.
Support supply chain managers with cost-to-serve and lane scenarios.
Work with project management specialists to evaluate logistics pilots.
skills_to_grow: Shipment identifiers, event semantics and financial reconciliation.
Deterministic validation, integrations and versioned calculation rules.
Cost allocation, sensitivity analysis and service trade-offs.
Evidence-based review of extracted carrier terms.
Pilot design, benefit measurement and facilitation.
Data access, retention, GDPR, applicable EU AI Act requirements and national consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a reusable lane review service that combines trusted shipment records, comparable carrier terms, cost recovery scenarios and measured pilots. Teams adapt connectors, definitions and approval limits to their own systems.
